author: Mark Magnier
description:
The Chinese-American community expressed anger and concern on Thursday over the death in custody of a Chinese national by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement [ICE] on US territory.
Lianyong Wei, 51, reportedly died in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) on August 23, although the scandal-plagued agency did not disclose the death until this week.
“Asian-Americans, Chinese-Americans, should be very concerned about this and very energised to stop what is essentially an...
title: Chinese-American community alarmed after China national dies in ICE custody

author: Vincent Chow
description:
The United States should start preparing for scenarios where extreme measures must be taken to stop China from achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI), according to a former White House official, including state-backed espionage and military strikes on Chinese data centres.
Jacob Stokes, deputy director of the Indo-Pacific Security Program at the Centre for a New American Security (CNAS), said at an online event on Thursday that various US agencies, including the Department of Defense...
title: US urged to consider military strikes to stop China achieving AGI first

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Former Ecuadorian president Lenin Moreno and a former Chinese ambassador to Quito asked the country’s highest court on Thursday to spare them the five-year sentences handed down last week over a US$76 million bribery scheme.
Moreno was convicted of bribery by a three-judge panel of the National Court of Justice over contracts for Ecuador’s largest hydroelectric project secured by a Chinese state contractor.
The judges found unanimously that he had used his position as vice-president, held from...
title: Ecuador’s ex-president and Chinese ambassador seek to avoid jail over belt and road dam

author: Zhang Tong
description:
A team of cybersecurity experts has announced they successfully compromised the latest Starlink user terminals, crossing the security boundaries of the world’s largest satellite constellation.
In a post on its social media account on Tuesday, Darknavy, an independent cybersecurity research institute headquartered in Singapore and Shanghai, said it had used sophisticated hardware attacks to gain full administrative control over the terminals, allowing it to run any custom code on the...
title: China-Singapore security team claims breakthrough in hacking Starlink terminals

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s cabinet approved a supplementary defence budget of NT$145.7 billion (US$4.6 billion) on Thursday, pushing the island’s total defence-related spending for this year above NT$1 trillion for the first time.
The additional funding is expected to raise this year’s overall defence spending from 3.32 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) to about 3.83 per cent, the highest level in decades.
The supplementary budget, which still requires legislative approval, is aimed at plugging gaps left...
title: Extra funds push Taiwan’s defence spending past NT$1 trillion for the first time

author: Carol Yang
description:
Mexico’s Foreign Affairs Secretary Roberto Velasco arrives in China on Sunday for his first official visit as his country navigates increasing US pressure to roll back Chinese trade ties.
The two-day visit will take place at the invitation of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said in Beijing on Thursday.
He said China expected the visit to be an opportunity to deepen mutual political trust and cooperation, and “promote the steady growth” of ties to better benefit...
title: Mexican foreign minister to meet Wang Yi in China as US demands trade ties rollback

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China’s military AI models trail their foreign equivalents in performance, concentrating on support functions rather than combat, according to a study by Chinese researchers.
The findings appeared in a paper by researchers affiliated with the Armed Police Force Shandong Corps and the Engineering University of People’s Armed Police, published in the journal Defence Industry Conversion in China in July.
“The military’s AI applications are mainly used in auxiliary fields such as intelligent...
title: Chinese military’s AI attack chain lags foreign models: researchers

author: Shi Huang
description:
One of the world’s most abundant rare earth elements could offer a comprehensive, long-lasting treatment for gout, a Chinese team has found.
The extremely painful form of inflammatory arthritis has plagued humanity for millennia. “No other pain is more severe than this, not iron screws, nor cords, nor the wound of a dagger, nor burning fire” – that is how the ancient Greek physician Aretaeus described the disease in the second century AD.
More than 55 million people worldwide had gout in 2020,...
title: China’s rare earth cerium drug can kill gout pains once and for all: scientists

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Washington is considering using Japanese, South Korean or Turkish frigate designs to expand the country’s naval fleet as the American shipbuilding industry struggles to meet demand, according to US media reports.
The move comes after President Donald Trump signed a National Security Presidential Memorandum on August 13 calling for the use of foreign shipbuilding capacity and investment.
However, the plan is likely to face strong opposition in Congress.
Potential contenders for the US Navy’s new...
title: US looks to warship designs from Japan, South Korea and Turkey, reports say

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
European Union and Chinese officials have been holding talks in Beijing ahead of the bloc’s October deadline for seeing “tangible results” in efforts to curb a trade deficit running at €1 billion-plus (US$1.2 billion) per day.
Denis Redonnet, the EU’s top trade enforcer, has led the European delegation, the South China Morning Post reported on Wednesday. The official has recently become the bloc’s point person for China trade, reflecting growing trade tensions and the possibility of a trade...
title: EU, China talk trade as Europe’s deadline for action looms

author: Fan Hou
description: People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng rejected criticism of China over global trade imbalances at the G20 finance meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. Below is the statement released by the Chinese central bank summarising the speech.
title: Chinese central bank chief’s remarks at G20

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
Xi Jinping has urged Middle Eastern nations to build a self-led security model, signalling a push to cut reliance on Washington following further US-Iran military clashes, although China’s president did not position Beijing as an alternative security guarantor.
On his first visit to Egypt in a decade, Xi made the proposal during talks with Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi at Cairo’s Ittihadiya Palace on Wednesday.
Analysts said the meeting reflected Egypt’s efforts to strengthen relations...
title: Xi Jinping’s call for Mideast to build own security framework is a message to US: expert

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Beijing said it conducted a routine patrol in waters east of Taiwan on Thursday, the latest in weeks of ramped-up activity by coastguard and other vessels that has alarmed the island.
China Coast Guard spokesman Jiang Lue said a formation led by the Putuoshan vessel carried out a “law enforcement” patrol “in accordance with the law”.
He said the formation had strengthened control over the waters since last month, safeguarding the rights and interests of Chinese citizens.
“The China Coast Guard...
title: Beijing ramps up coastguard patrols and scientific surveys near Taiwan

author: Carol Yang
description:
Glaciers on the Tibetan Plateau are likely to become more unstable, which may lead to more collapses and collateral disasters, a senior climate official warns as the death toll from last week’s catastrophic landslide and flood on the China-Nepal border continues to rise.
“Over the past 60 years, the glacier area on the Tibetan Plateau has shrunk by around 24 per cent, with around 7,000 small glaciers disappearing completely,” Gao Rong, deputy director of China’s National Climate Centre, told a...
title: Unstable Tibetan Plateau risks cascading disasters as glacier losses mount in Nepal, China

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday accused the Donald Trump administration of using the critical minerals contest with China as an excuse for corruption – alleging billions of dollars in deals were enriching the president’s family and friends.
“Competition with China is no excuse for abandoning safeguards that prevent taxpayer funds from being misused for private enrichment,” said Linda Sanchez, the Democratic lawmaker from California, at a Ways and Means Committee hearing titled “Strategic...
title: China rivalry ‘no excuse’: US Democrats allege corruption in Trump’s mining deals

author: Shi Huang
description:
Four Chinese academics who lost posts at leading universities after a high-profile blogger flagged their research for misconduct have come under official investigation by China’s leading funder of basic research.
The National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) published details on August 26 of 31 new misconduct cases at universities and hospitals across China, involving more than 40 researchers – its largest such public disclosure to date.
Among them were four prominent professors...
title: China launches largest-ever academic misconduct crackdown after Student Geng scandal
